results.title: Quibi - Wikipedia
results.snippet: Quibi (/ ˈkwɪbi / KWIB-ee) was an American short-form streaming platform that generated content for viewing on mobile devices. It was founded in Los Angeles in August 2018 as NewTV by Jeffrey Katzenberg, and it was led by Meg Whitman as CEO. The service raised $1.75 billion from investors. results.title: Quibi: what happened, and why it shut down | Looks Back
results.snippet: Quibi was a mobile-only streaming service for short premium video, founded by Jeffrey Katzenberg with Meg Whitman as CEO. It raised $1.75 billion, launched on 6 April 2020, announced its shutdown six months later, and went dark on 1 December 2020, one of the fastest and most expensive failures in tech history.

results.title: Quibi officially announces it's shutting down - CNBC
results.snippet: Quibi, the short-form entertainment service for mobile devices, announced on Wednesday that it will shut down, just over six months after its service launched.

results.title: Quibi: What is it, why did it fail and what comes next? - CNET
results.snippet: Wednesday, Quibi confirmed it is shutting down. The service itself will go dark on or around Dec. 1, Quibi said Thursday on its customer support page. Quibi would be a risky bet even in normal times.

results.title: Quibi Sets Shutdown Date - The Hollywood Reporter
results.snippet: Quibi Sets Shutdown Date Quibi expects to shut down "on or about Dec. 1," according to a new post on the mobile video startup's customer service page.

results.snippet: The Quibi app as of Dec. 1 is no longer operable, marking the quick and quiet end of Jeffrey Katzenberg's ill-fated $1.75 billion quest.

ofrenda.calavera:
Quick bites, big stories, movie-quality art,
But subscribers failed to play their part.
Designed for the phone, a dream framed so neat,
Now Quibi rests peacefully in a digital sheet.
